1. Overview & Motivation

In cinematic mathematical animation engines, audio—specifically spoken narration—is the core pedagogical driver that guides viewer focus through complex proofs, algorithmic state transitions, and geometric derivations.
Historically, web animation frameworks relied on:

items: **Third-Party Cloud APIs** (ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google Cloud TTS): Requiring API keys, incurring continuous network latency (500–2,000ms), and preventing offline or air-gapped video rendering.

**Browser Native `SpeechSynthesis` API**: Lacking deterministic audio buffer outputs, offering poor voice quality, and providing no direct access to raw PCM samples for spectrum visualization or audio muxing in headless MP4/WebM video export.

blocks.text: Retiam introduces a **Decoupled Dual-Engine Text-To-Speech Suite** via `retiam/tts` ([libs/tts/index.ts](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/index.ts)):

children: Executes the 82-million parameter model directly in browser GPU shaders via ONNX Runtime Web.
100% offline asset sovereignty with model weights stored locally in [`public/models/kokoro/`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/public/models/kokoro).
28 studio voices across American and British English.
Zero model weight downloads, instant synthesis with access to **320+ natural neural voices** across 70+ languages.

Dual-runtime design: in-process execution for Node.js (CLI rendering, unit tests, scripts) and proxy routing through local Vite development server middleware (`/api/tts/msedge/synthesize`) for browsers.
Precision word boundary timing extraction for synchronized closed captions and subtitle highlighting.
3Blue1Brown-style explainer narration voice persona (`en-US-AndrewNeural` at `0.96x` speed with beat pauses).
Automatic voiceover ducking on Retiam's [`AudioManager`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/audio/AudioManager.ts).
Word boundary subtitle synchronization with [`Subtitles`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/components/Subtitles.ts).
Entity speech micro-animations with [`TTSNarrationComponent`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/components/TTSNarrationComponent.ts).

Declarative animation via [`Speak`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/animations/Speak.ts) and helper [`speak()`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/animations/Speak.ts#L186).

blocks.text: 3. Local-First Asset Architecture (public/models/kokoro/)
To guarantee privacy, eliminate rate limits, and enable completely offline animation authoring and headless rendering, all model assets are downloaded once and stored locally inside the project.

blocks.text: Git Sovereignty & GitHub File Size Management

Because raw neural network weights (`model.onnx` is 310.45 MB and `model_q8f16.onnx` is 82.05 MB) exceed GitHub's 100 MB single-file push limit and bloat git clone operations, **model weights are excluded from Git** via `.gitignore`:

blocks.code:
# Local ML/AI Model Caches (weights downloaded on-demand and cached locally)
public/models/*
!public/models/.gitkeep

blocks.text: Automated On-Demand Download & Local Drive Caching ([tools/viteKokoroPlugin.ts](../tools/viteKokoroPlugin.ts))

Instead of requiring manual weight setup or checking massive binaries into Git, Retiam incorporates an automated Vite server plugin (`kokoroModelServerPlugin`) active during development (`npm run dev`) and production preview (`npm run serve`):

items: **Frontend Request Interception**:

blocks.text: When the browser / Web Studio initializes TTS, Transformers.js requests model assets (`/models/kokoro/config.json`, `/models/kokoro/tokenizer.json`, `/models/kokoro/onnx/model.onnx`, or `/models/kokoro/voices/${voice}.bin`).

items: **Local Drive Availability Check**:

blocks.text: The Vite middleware inspects the local filesystem (`public/models/kokoro/<asset>`):

items: **If Available Locally**: The server immediately serves the file directly from the local drive with full HTTP Range request support (`HTTP 206 Partial Content`) and persistent caching (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`). Zero external network requests are made.

**If Missing Locally**: The middleware intercepts the 404 condition, fetches the asset from the upstream Hugging Face repository (`https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX/resolve/main/<asset>`), streams it into a `.tmp` file, and atomically commits it to `public/models/kokoro/<asset>` on the local drive.
**Seamless Direct Serving**:

blocks.text: Once cached to the local drive, the file is piped directly to the frontend's pending request.

items: **Subsequent Invocations**:

blocks.text: All future requests find the asset already present on disk, ensuring 100% offline, zero-latency local execution.

items: **In-Flight Concurrency Protection**:

blocks.text: A mutex map (`inFlightDownloads`) prevents duplicate downloads or race conditions when parallel frontend threads request the same model file simultaneously.
Zero-Remote Network Execution Mechanism

items: **Local Model Configuration**:

blocks.text: [`KokoroWebGPUProvider`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/providers/KokoroWebGPUProvider.ts) explicitly configures Transformers.js environment flags:

items: **Local Voice Interception (Browser Cache Pre-seeding)**:

blocks.text: In the browser, `kokoro-js` internally queries `caches.open("kokoro-voices")` matching the Hugging Face URI. Before synthesis, `ensureVoiceCached(voice)` intercepts this:

items: Fetches the local file `/models/kokoro/voices/${voice}.bin` directly from the local Vite dev/preview server.
Puts the response into `kokoro-voices` under the expected Hugging Face key.
When the underlying tokenizer checks the cache, it finds the local buffer instantly with **zero external HTTP requests**.
**Headless Node.js Execution & Pre-fetching**:

blocks.text: In Node.js environments (CLI video rendering), `ensureKokoroModelOnDisk` can be invoked programmatically to pre-populate any required ONNX weights and voice vectors directly from Hugging Face into `public/models/kokoro/`.
Upfront Offline Pre-fetching ([tools/downloadkokoromodel.mjs](../tools/downloadkokoromodel.mjs))
For air-gapped workstations, CI/CD runners, or users who want to download all weights upfront in a single batch before going offline, Retiam provides a dedicated CLI pre-fetch script:

blocks.code:
npm run tts:download
# Or execute directly:
node tools/download_kokoro_model.mjs

blocks.text: This script verifies if local assets already exist, and streams any missing core assets (`config.json`, `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, `onnx/model_q8f16.onnx`, and `onnx/model.onnx`) directly into [`public/models/kokoro/`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/public/models/kokoro) with real-time transfer progress.
4. Subsystem Implementations
A. Core Types & Interfaces ([core/types.ts](../libs/tts/core/types.ts))
The library defines strict TypeScript interfaces for model configurations, voice profiles, and output payloads:
B. Audio Container & WAV Encoder ([core/TTSAudio.ts](../libs/tts/core/TTSAudio.ts))
Kokoro synthesizes audio as a raw 1D array of single-channel, 32-bit floating point PCM samples $[-1.0, 1.0]$ at a fixed sampling rate of **24,000 Hz**.
The `TTSAudio` class wraps these samples and provides conversions:

items: **`toAudioBuffer(context?)`**: Directly instantiates a native Web Audio `AudioBuffer` and sets channel data without re-encoding to WAV, minimizing CPU overhead.
**`encodeWAV(samples, sampleRate)`**: A standalone 16-bit PCM RIFF WAV encoder that builds valid RIFF/WAVE chunks with little-endian integer clamping:
**`toBlob()` / `toDataUrl()` / `toObjectUrl()`**: Generates download links, base64 strings, or temporary object URLs.

**`play(audioManager?, options?)`**: Automatically routes playback through Retiam's `AudioManager` on the voiceover bus, applying BGM volume ducking ramps and returning a promise that resolves when speech concludes.

blocks.text: D. LRU Utterance Cache ([core/TTSCache.ts](../libs/tts/core/TTSCache.ts))
Animation authoring in Web Studio involves constant timeline scrubbing, scene re-running, and hot reloading. Re-running neural inference on identical sentences wastes GPU cycles.
`TTSCache` provides an $O(1)$ LRU cache:

items: **Key Schema**: `${voice}:${speed.toFixed(2)}:${text.trim().toLowerCase()}`
**Eviction**: When `maxSize` (default: 128) is reached, the oldest utterance is evicted, revoking its temporary Object URL to prevent browser memory leaks.

blocks.text: E. WebGPU Provider Implementation ([providers/KokoroWebGPUProvider.ts](../libs/tts/providers/KokoroWebGPUProvider.ts))
The provider encapsulates all low-level ONNX Runtime Web and hardware negotiation:

children: Queries `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()`.
If WebGPU is supported, initializes with `device: "webgpu"` and `dtype: "fp32"`.
If WebGPU is unavailable (e.g. older hardware or mobile browser without flags), gracefully falls back to `device: "wasm"` with `dtype: "q8"`.

items: **Inference Pipeline**:

children: Exposes `async *stream(text, options)` using sentence splitting regexes to yield `TTSStreamChunk` objects sequentially for real-time progressive playback.

6. Microsoft Edge Neural TTS Provider (MsEdgeTTSProvider)
The `MsEdgeTTSProvider` implements `ITTSProvider` with a dual-runtime architecture:
1. Dual-Runtime Execution Strategy

items: **Node.js Runtime** (CLI rendering, headless export, unit tests):

blocks.text: Directly executes `msedge-tts` in-process via WebSockets with authentic Edge Read Aloud client headers.

items: **Browser Runtime** (Vite development server & Web Studio):

blocks.text: Modern browsers block custom WebSocket `Origin` and `User-Agent` headers. The browser provider seamlessly proxies requests via the local Vite middleware (`/api/tts/msedge/synthesize`), which generates the audio server-side and streams it to the client with `X-Word-Boundaries` and `X-Audio-Duration-Ms` response headers.
2. Zero-Dependency MP3 Metadata Parser ([libs/tts/core/mp3Utils.ts](../libs/tts/core/mp3Utils.ts))

Calculates exact utterance durations, frame counts, and sample rates (24,000 Hz) directly from MPEG-1/2 Layer III bitstream headers in pure TypeScript, without requiring native decoding dependencies in Node.
3. Prosody & Volume Normalization

items: **Rate**: Multiplier `speed` is converted into an Edge SSML rate string: `speed = 0.96` becomes `"-4%"`.

**Volume**: Standard normalized floating-point numbers in `[0.0, 1.0]` (e.g. `1.0`) are automatically translated into `[0, 100]` percentage integers (e.g. `100`), ensuring full studio loudness without clipping or attenuation.
**Pitch**: SSML pitch shifts such as `"+0Hz"` or `"+5st"`.

items.text: **Curated Catalog**: Pre-registered in [`libs/tts/core/MsEdgeVoices.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/libs/tts/core/MsEdgeVoices.ts) with premier voices:
children: `en-US-AndrewNeural` (Warm, authentic university professor / documentary narrator)
`en-US-JennyNeural` (Warm, conversational, natural)
`en-US-GuyNeural` (Confident, broadcast, instructional)
`en-US-AriaNeural`, `en-US-AvaNeural`, `en-US-EmmaNeural`, `en-US-BrianNeural`
`en-GB-SoniaNeural`, `en-GB-RyanNeural`, `zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`, `ja-JP-NanamiNeural`

items: **Dynamic Fetching**: `fetchRemoteMsEdgeVoices()` retrieves the complete live catalog of 322+ voices from the upstream Azure Read Aloud endpoint on demand.
**Open Union Typing**: `MsEdgeVoiceId = ... | (string & {})` gives full IDE autocomplete while permitting any valid voice ID without TypeScript compiler errors.

Automated test suites verify both providers end-to-end:

blocks.text: Verified Edge TTS Test Cases ([test/msedgettstest.ts](../test/msedgettstest.ts)):

items: **Catalog & Discovery**: 32 curated voices, gender, locale, Grade A+ ratings, short name mapping.
**MP3 Frame Parser & Word Boundaries**: 24,000 Hz sample rate detection, duration accuracy, word timing verification.
**TTSAudio MP3 Container**: Base64 data URI output, MIME type handling, duration properties.
**Client Provider Switching**: Seamless runtime switching between `msedge-tts` and `kokoro-webgpu`.
**Global TTS Facade**: Static helpers (`TTS.msedge`, `TTS.useProvider`).
**Speak Animation & Options**: Timeline duration locking, speed multiplier, ducking.
**Progressive Sentence Streaming**: Progressive chunk generator with monotonic offset tracking.
